entry.name: Mary T. Thanh Hai
entry.department: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Office of New Drugs

evidence.currentRole: https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/center-drug-evaluation-and-research-cder/mary-thanh-hai — “Director - Office of New Drugs”. Individual FDA biography identifies a career FDA clinical-research leader, employed at FDA since 1998. Her office oversees clinical/nonclinical investigations and advises on preapproval and postapproval studies, including clinical trial safety and interpretation. This meets the federal scientific research-leadership route rather than an ordinary administrative-support role.
evidence.doctorateOrPapers: https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/center-drug-evaluation-and-research-cder/mary-thanh-hai — Employer identifies her as an MD, an internist/endocrinologist, and says her medical degree is from Georgetown University. MD is used under the clinical-research exception; phdInstitution maps the qualifying medical doctorate, not a claim that she earned a PhD. No degree year stated.
evidence.vietnameseSignal: https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/center-drug-evaluation-and-research-cder/mary-thanh-hai — Published full name includes the Vietnamese name token Thanh in Thanh Hai, an affirmative name signal beyond a shared surname alone. No diacritics or expanded initial reconstructed.

coverage.employer: NIH Intramural Research Program — all institutes including NCI
coverage.note: Opened and scanned full alphabetical all-institute PI directory, including given-name tokens and uncommon surnames. Three Vietnamese-name investigators resolved to existing IDs. Ambiguous Haiming Cao, Qing Lan, Claire Le Pichon and Hung Chang Yao were not inferred Vietnamese. Later-pass searches emphasized Thanh, Huong, Dung, Linh, Thuy, Quang, Thao, Hien, Ngoc, Tuan, Hanh, Phuong, Minh, Viet, Hieu, Khanh, Khoa, Chau, Thu, Bao, Truc, Hai, Hoan, Tri, Huy, Tuyet, Lien, Bich, Huyen, Nhan, Oanh, Phuc, Tram, Nhung, Tung, Nghia, Chinh, Diem, Uyen, Kiet, Quoc, Toan, Binh and Tien; supplementary less-common-surname searches covered Phung, Diep, Dinh, Luu, Luong, Quach, Ton, Thai, Vuong, Bach, Dao, Doan, Lai and Tieu. Search results were discovery leads only. No new NIH candidate cleared every test. Coverage is a broad discovery pass, not a census of all 1,200 PIs’ lab members.

coverage.employer: Other NIH institutes — NIAID, NIDDK, NINDS, NHGRI, NIAMS, NIA, NIDA and NIDCR
coverage.note: Supplementary targeted employer-domain given-name/staff-scientist searches; central PI directory supplies all-institute coverage. Results largely consisted of grants to external universities, publications, program analysts, IT staff, trainees or prior proposals. These searches are not claimed as direct full-directory inspection. NHGRI Nicholas Nguyen is an MHS/PA-C program analyst, NIDDK Nicole Nguyen is a postbac alumna, and NIAMS Oanh/Thien Nguyen leads are IT branch staff in employer search results. None accepted from snippets.

Deeper NCTR coverage: followed index to full alphabetical investigator-name list and inspected it, beyond w1 landing-page extraction. No affirmative Vietnamese-name PI emerged. CDER/CBER/CTP given-name and less-common-surname searches found Mary T. Thanh Hai, verified on her individual FDA page. Most other hits were application correspondence, regulatory pharmacists/project managers, external speakers or papers, not current individual scientist profiles. Research-biographies guessed landing URL failed and was not used. NCTR all-biosketch download returned unsupported Word content type; alphabetical index remained usable.
